clue.text: Self-important, if concerned with the paper game?

definitions.meaning: an older sense describes a pompous person who gives himself airs
Consequences is a parlour game played by passing round a folded sheet of paper

explanation.surface: A pompous person is mocked as though he were obsessed with a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: Consequences is a parlour game in which players write lines of a story on a folded sheet of paper, so the adjective also means 'to do with that game'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: pompous and self-satisfied in an older usage, and relating to the paper parlour game Consequences.

clue.text: Expenses of excursions ?

explanation.surface: A question about the cost of day trips.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the word in two parts and it describes trips out.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent is expenditure, and goings-out are trips or outings.

clue.text: That daughter of the voice of God !

definitions.text: That daughter of the voice of God

parts.words: That daughter of the voice of God
parts.note: the opening line of Wordsworth's Ode to Duty, with its first word replaced by 'That'

explanation.surface: An exclamation from a poem addressing Duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's Ode to Duty begins '___ Daughter of the Voice of God!'; 'That' stands in for the missing adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth calls Duty a severe daughter of God's voice, and the missing word means strict.

clue.text: Whither ? North, Mum, as of yore

parts.note: quo is Latin for whither, as in quo vadis
a dam is a mother, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A question of where to go put to an old-fashioned mother.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin adverb means former or formerly, describing what once was.

clue.text: The old Turk is out-of-date

parts.note: the Turkish courtesy title for an educated man was abolished in 1934, so it is out of date

explanation.surface: An old Turkish man is behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old Turk' is a title of respect used in the Ottoman Empire, dropped by law in modern Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: This Ottoman title of respect, like 'sir', was officially abolished in republican Turkey.

clue.text: Belt that ensures passion is restrained!

definitions.text: Belt that ensures passion is restrained

parts.words: Belt that ensures passion is restrained
parts.note: a climate belt between tropics and polar regions whose name also means moderate in passion

explanation.surface: A garment meant to curb desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' suggests a garment, but it is a climatic zone, and the zone's name also describes someone keeping temper in check.
explanation.definitionFit: The mild climatic zone shares its name with the adjective for moderate and self-controlled.

clue.text: No doubt they are still beloved of violinists

definitions.text: No doubt they are still beloved of violinists

parts.words: No doubt they are still beloved of violinists
parts.note: the Cremona family's violins remain prized, and their name is Italian for 'beloved' ones

explanation.surface: A remark that certain things remain dear to string players.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cremona family of violin makers had a name that is the Italian plural for 'loved'.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments by the Cremona violin-making family are still treasured, and the name means 'loved' in Italian.

clue.text: Jet fighter ? No, says Goethe's young heroine

parts.note: MiG is the Russian make of jet fighter aircraft
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A girl from Goethe refuses to be called a fighter plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine is the waif in Goethe's novel Wilhelm Meister's Apprenticeship.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the mysterious girl in Goethe's Wilhelm Meister, later the subject of Thomas's opera.

clue.text: The more affluent punter has set out

parts.note: a punter is someone who places bets, a gambler
to be off is to have set out or departed

explanation.surface: A richer gambler has headed off somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a more prosperous position is an idiom for having more money.

clue.text: Became a father — but where to look for charity ?

definitions.meaning: a biblical past tense meaning fathered a child
split into two words it is where you seek alms, at a door

explanation.surface: A new father wonders where to find help.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as 'beg at': the place one goes to ask for alms.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic past tense of beget means fathered, and split it says where one asks for alms.

clue.text: Where that operatic heroine gets round one!

indicators.note: the heroine's name encircles the single letter, so she is said to go round it

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An opera heroine manages to persuade somebody somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' is the whole definition: the answer is a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida city is a place, so it answers the question word asking for a location.

clue.text: Here, where men sit and hear each other (Keats)

definitions.text: Here, where men sit and hear each other (Keats)

parts.words: Here, where men sit and hear each other (Keats)
parts.note: a line from Keats's Ode to a Nightingale with its last word left blank, as the printed page shows with a dash

explanation.surface: A quotation from Keats about men sitting together and listening to one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash after 'other': the clue is a fill-in-the-blank from Ode to a Nightingale, whose line ends with the sound of men lamenting.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word of the quoted line is a low sound of pain, which completes Keats's picture of suffering humanity.

clue.text: Four-footed Beau Brummel ? Pretty weedy !

definitions.meaning: Beau Brummell was a famous Regency dandy, so a four-footed one is a dandy lion
a pretty weed with yellow flowers

explanation.surface: A fashionable creature turns out to be rather feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays on the sound of the name: a dandy lion. The second takes 'weedy' literally: the plant is a pretty weed.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow lawn weed's name sounds like a foppish big cat, and it is a common but attractive garden weed.

clue.text: So much French spirit produces rage

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Too much French liquor leads to fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of temper is a burst of childish rage.

clue.text: Her Grace's were phenomenal at the tea-table

definitions.text: Her Grace's were phenomenal at the tea-table

parts.words: Her Grace's were phenomenal at the tea-table
parts.note: a duchess's hungry stomach noises heard over tea

explanation.surface: A duchess makes a remarkable impression at tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her Grace' is a duchess; the noises in question are those of a hungry stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Low growling noises from an empty stomach are the deep sounds heard at the table.

clue.text: Rossini's girl in Algiers

parts.note: the clue names Rossini's comic opera about a girl in Algiers with one word of its title left out

explanation.surface: A reference to the heroine of a Rossini opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Rossini's opera is L'italiana in Algeri, in English 'The ___ Girl in Algiers'; the missing word is her nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The opera's heroine Isabella comes from Italy, which gives the title its adjective.

clue.text: Gate-crashing into ruins, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of the two words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A party gate-crasher leaves a place in a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges INTO RUINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcing one's way in uninvited is an unwelcome entry.

clue.text: Old South African hunter, not a taverner

definitions.meaning: the San people of southern Africa were traditionally hunter-gatherers
an old tavern hung out a bush as its sign; the clue says that sense is not meant

explanation.surface: A hunter from old South Africa, who was no innkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good wine needs no bush': taverns once hung a bush of ivy outside, so the word could describe an innkeeper. The 'not' steers you to the hunter instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The San hunter-gatherers were formerly called by this name, which could also describe a keeper of a tavern with a bush sign.

clue.text: Don't be so beastly, but " Be a hero in the strife'!" (Longfellow)

definitions.text: Don't be so beastly, but " Be a hero in the strife'!" (Longfellow)

parts.words: Don't be so beastly, but " Be a hero in the strife'!" (Longfellow)
parts.note: Longfellow's Psalm of Life says 'Be not like dumb, driven cattle! Be a hero in the strife!'

explanation.surface: A rousing call to stop being horrid and fight bravely.
explanation.walkthrough: The line before Longfellow's quoted one is 'Be not like dumb, driven cattle!': 'beastly' means like cattle, not nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being like dull driven cattle is to be cow-like and sluggish.

clue.text: Francois, naked and spotless, is of this age !

parts.note: a Frenchman would say nu for naked
clear, free from marks

explanation.surface: A naked, clean-living Frenchman is thoroughly modern.
explanation.walkthrough: The French name signals that 'naked' is in French. The definition refers to the atomic age.
explanation.definitionFit: The twentieth century was often called the atomic age, so this adjective describes the present era.

clue.text: What the coiffeur's handmaid did after the hairdo ?

definitions.text: What the coiffeur's handmaid did after the hairdo

parts.words: What the coiffeur's handmaid did after the hairdo
parts.note: the assistant cleared the cut hair from the floor, and the phrase also names an upswept hairstyle

explanation.surface: The hairdresser's assistant tidies up once the styling is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: the assistant brushed the clippings into a pile, and the hairdo itself was combed upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: After a haircut the floor is brushed clean, and an upswept style is one combed high on the head.

clue.text: Cats in a panic are apt to be fiendish

indicators.note: a panic throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Frightened cats behave like devils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'panic' rearranges the letters of CATS IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish behaviour is like that of the Devil, Satan.

clue.text: Perhaps this poor outcast's re ward is in the sky?…

definitions.text: Perhaps this poor outcast's re ward is in the sky

parts.words: Perhaps this poor outcast's re ward is in the sky
parts.note: a stray pariah dog's only reward may be pie in the sky, and the first part sounds like that pie

explanation.surface: A wretched outcast is promised a heavenly reward.
explanation.walkthrough: A pariah dog is an ownerless stray in India; 'pie in the sky' is an empty promise, and the dog's name begins with that sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The ownerless stray dogs of Asian villages are outcasts, and their name begins like 'pie'.

clue.text: To wit it's usually brief

parts.note: the Latin word is normally written in its short form, viz

explanation.surface: A remark that wit is best kept short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brevity is the soul of wit' is the false trail; the Latin adverb meaning 'namely' is usually abbreviated to viz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin adverb means namely, which is the sense of the old phrase introducing an example.

clue.text: … but this animal is doing a good turn

indicators.note: a turn round of the letters is what is meant, not a kind deed

explanation.surface: A creature does somebody a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good turn' looks like a kind deed but rearranges DOING. The ellipsis links back to 20, another dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian wild dog is an animal, like the outcast in the previous clue.

clue.text: 18 holes precede one at the 19th

definitions.meaning: a full game of golf covers eighteen holes
the nineteenth hole is the clubhouse bar, where someone buys drinks for everyone

explanation.surface: A golfer's day: the course comes before a drink in the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'nineteenth hole' is golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar, where one person pays for a set of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A full game of golf and a set of drinks bought for a group are both called by this word.

clue.text: Browning's Ben Ezra

parts.note: Robert Browning's poem is titled with Ben Ezra's religious title in front of his name

explanation.surface: A character from a Browning poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is 'Rabbi Ben Ezra' ('Grow old along with me!'); the missing word is the man's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Ezra was a Jewish teacher, and the poem gives him that religious title.

clue.text: Not that she was of the enclosed order!

definitions.text: Not that she was of the enclosed order

parts.words: Not that she was of the enclosed order
parts.note: the famous French courtesan's surname, de Lenclos, sounds like 'of the enclosed', though she was no cloistered nun

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain woman was certainly no nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Ninon de Lenclos was a celebrated 17th-century French courtesan: by name she was 'of l'Enclos', but hardly a member of an enclosed religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtesan de Lenclos carried a surname meaning 'the enclosure', yet led a life far from a convent's.

clue.text: Is Ben long in sending one upstairs ?

annotationWithheld.why: Is Ben long in sending one upstairs ? (9): the letters of BEN LONG IN give the answer, but no word is left to signal the anagram; 'sending' is needed in the definition 'sending one upstairs'
annotationWithheld.clue: Is Ben long in sending one upstairs ?

clue.text: Meaningful buildings

parts.note: the word means both interpretations put on words and things that have been built

explanation.surface: A phrase about architecture with significance.
explanation.walkthrough: One word covers both senses: the meaning one puts on a statement, and an erected structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpretations of a text and erected structures share this one plural noun.
